sources.title: Taiwan holds local elections under Beijing's watchful gaze
Polls open in Taiwan's closely watched local elections

en.title: Taiwan holds local elections under Beijing's watchful gaze
en.dek: Voters across 22 cities and counties cast ballots in Saturday's vote as Chinese authorities weigh in on the race
facts: Taiwan is electing local leaders across 22 cities and counties on Saturday
Chinese authorities have repeatedly weighed in on the race
Campaigners have focused on issues like transport and childcare
Polls opened Saturday morning as reported by DW
The election is described as closely watched by international outlets
Voting is taking place under global media scrutiny
body: Voters across 22 cities and counties cast ballots in Saturday's local election, with polling stations opening Saturday morning according to DW.
Chinese authorities have repeatedly weighed in on the race, as noted by France 24, while campaigners have focused their platforms on issues like transport and childcare.
Polls opened Saturday morning as confirmed by DW's reporting from the scene.
The election is taking place under Beijing's watchful gaze, with Chinese authorities making repeated interventions in the campaign.
Campaigners have focused their platforms on issues like transport and childcare, according to France 24's report on the race.
The vote is described as closely watched by international media, with both France 24 and DW covering the event extensively.
Voters are participating in a contest that has drawn significant attention from Chinese authorities throughout the campaign period.
The election marks another instance of local voting in Taiwan occurring amid Beijing's ongoing political scrutiny.
en.context: Taiwan is holding local elections to select leaders across its 22 cities and counties, with the vote drawing attention from Chinese authorities who have repeatedly weighed in on the race according to international reporting.
